To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
SARS CoV-2 spike glycoproteins share a number of minimal immune determinants with human oogenesis related proteins.
SARS CoV-2 shares 41 pentapeptides with 27 human oogenesis related proteins.
SARS CoV-2 spike protein shares 41 pentapeptides with proteins that are involved in oogenesis.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the potential effects of SARS Cov 2 infection on the female reproductive system and the generation of autoantibodies in infected patients.
the identification of SARS Co V 2 derived epitopes that might be involved in the production of crossreactive auto-antibodies that could lead to infertility and/or the onset of autoimmune diseases.
the possible effects of molecular mimicry in SARS Cov 2 infection on the female reproductive system and fertility.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
SARS CoV2 infection may be a cause of female infertility.

molecular mimicry may play a role in female infertility in SARS Co V 2 infected patients by leading to the production, by the adaptive immune system, of autoantibodies that target oogenesis related proteins.

the molecular mimicry between SACS CoV 2 protein epitopes and oogenesis related human proteins may lead to the generation of crossreactive autoimmunity, which in turn could contribute to the onset of female infertility.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
molecular mimicry between Sars CoV 2 viral proteins and oogenesis proteins could contribute to the onset of autoantibodies that could interfere with female fertility.
SARS CoV2 spike protein shares a large number of minimal immune determinants with proteins involved in oogenesis, utero-placental development, and decidualization.
the spike protein of SARS Co V 2 is capable of generating crossreactive antibodies with the potential to cause damage to the female reproductive tissues and to interfere with oogenesis.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the molecular mimicry phenomenon between SARS Co V2 proteins and ogenesis related proteins could contribute to the onset of deleterious crossreactive autoimmunity in infected women, which could lead to female infertility.
SARS CoV2 spike glycoproteins and oogenesis proteins are sharing linear sequences that could be recognized by the immune system of infected women.

SARS CoV-2 spike protein shares a significant number of immunogenic epitopes with human proteins involved in oogenesis and female fertility, which might contribute to the onset of autoimmune diseases in infected patients.
